en.ti: Why do the keys of Continue, opencode and Kilo go in their file?
en.x: why do the keys of continue, opencode and kilo go in their file? because they cannot ask for it with a command, as claude code and codex can. tramtai writes it in their file, inside your user folder; it is the key of their own api, which works nowhere else.

en.ti: Why can’t I turn a tool on?
en.x: why can’t i turn a tool on? the row says why. tools are not offered in server mode or with tramtai’s own https, and the agent must be allowed for apps. if it is on in another workspace, turn it off there first.

en.ti: Can I turn a tool on for just one project?
en.x: can i turn a tool on for just one project? only claude code, from the project workspace: it writes to .claude/settings.local.json and never to settings.json, which is shared through git. the others, from the global workspace.

en.ti: Why does Tramtai ask me to move Continue to config.yaml?
en.x: why does tramtai ask me to move continue to config.yaml? continue reads config.yaml if it exists and config.json if not. with only config.json, creating the yaml would leave your json unused: move it to config.yaml and turn the tool on again.

en.ti: What if it says config.toml already has a “tramtai” provider?
en.x: what if it says config.toml already has a “tramtai” provider? tramtai did not write that table, or an old one was left after editing the file by hand. rename or delete it. a model or model provider on several lines does not work either: put it on one line.

en.ti: What if I change Codex’s model with /model?
en.x: what if i change codex’s model with /model? that line becomes yours: when you turn the tool off, tramtai does not put it back as it was. if you want another model, change it in config.toml.

en.ti: What if I edit a tool’s file by hand?
en.x: what if i edit a tool’s file by hand? turning off removes only what is still as tramtai wrote it and leaves the rest. if you change its part, the row becomes “out of date”. an unreadable file is not touched: the row says what to do.

en.ti: What if I already have an API with the tool’s name?
en.x: what if i already have an api with the tool’s name? tramtai does not touch it and does not turn the tool on: rename it in my apis and turn the tool on again.

en.ti: What is “tramtai tools key” for?
en.x: what is “tramtai tools key” for? claude code and codex use it to ask for their key. it responds while tramtai keeps the key (on or turned off, not after “forget”) and prints only the key; turned off, its stopped api rejects it.

en.ti: Which commands does the CLI have?
en.x: which commands does the cli have? tramtai herramientas (or tools): listar (list), activar (enable), desactivar (disable), olvidar (forget), restaurar (restore) and clave (key).

en.ti: How do I turn several on or off at once?
en.x: how do i turn several on or off at once? pass several ids or --all, for example “tramtai tools enable --all”. enable takes --model with agent/model, such as claude/sonnet.

en.ti: Files
en.x: files tramtai turns your pdf, word, excel and other documents into text before handing them to the agent. your app sends it through the native api, uploading it to /cargas; through openai or anthropic, in base64 inside the message. tramtai keeps it as an upload identified by its content: the same file is never stored twice. turns it into text markitdown turns pdf, word, powerpoint, excel and html into markdown; text goes as is. hands it to the agent one delimited block per file, with your message. the agent does not read your disk. you get the response like any other request, in the format of the api you used. native api: upload each file with post /cargas and create the request citing its uploads. openai or anthropic: put the file in base64 inside the message (file, input file or document). in the playground you can attach them too, to see the response first. pdf, .docx, .pptx, .xlsx and html are converted; .txt, .md, .markdown, .json, .jsonl, .csv, .tsv, .xml, .yaml, .yml, .toml, .ini and .log go as is. no zip. native api: up to 50 mb per file and 20 per request; converted, up to 20 mb of text. openai and anthropic: about 12 mb in total. details: /api/v1/limites.

en.ti: Can I send images?
en.x: can i send images? not yet. through openai and anthropic the file goes inside the message: tramtai does not download urls or use file id.

en.ti: Why was my request rejected for its size?
en.x: why was my request rejected for its size? what the agent would get does not fit the model. send fewer pages or split the file; the log says which one weighs most. no tokens are spent.

en.ti: What if the converter is missing?
en.x: what if the converter is missing? settings → files → “prepare files”, or “tramtai converter prepare”. if your network blocks the download, use the converter package for windows.

en.ti: Does anything leave my computer when converting?
en.x: does anything leave my computer when converting? no: markitdown runs on your computer. the converted text goes to the agent, like any message.

en.ti: The file could not be converted
en.x: the file could not be converted conversion fallida a file could not be converted. check that it is not damaged or password-protected and that its format is accepted.

en.ti: The file converter is missing
en.x: the file converter is missing conversor no disponible the file converter is missing: settings → files → “prepare files”. if your network blocks the download, use the converter package for windows.

en.ti: The input does not fit in the model
en.x: the input does not fit in the model entrada demasiado grande the documents do not fit the model. send fewer pages, split the file or put a model with more context in the fallback.

en.ti: JSON responses
en.x: json responses ask for the response in a fixed shape (a json schema) and tramtai validates it before handing it over. the schema the fields and their type, built from templates or in json. the agent answers following the requested shape. validation tramtai checks every field, formats too: date, email, url… correction if it does not match, it can ask the same agent to fix it, up to 3 times. in the playground, open “recipe options” and turn on “shaped response”. pick a template (extract data, classify, summary, tasks…) or add your fields with their type and description. test it: if it does not match, you will see which field failed and the “correct” button. in “if the response does not match” ask for up to 3 automatic corrections; each one is another request. click “save as api”: your app will always get that shape. through openai the schema goes in response format; through the native api, in salida. if the response does not match, you get 422 salida no cumple esquema.

en.ti: Are formats checked?
en.x: are formats checked? yes: date, date-time, email, url… a date-time without a time zone does not match “date-time”.

en.ti: Can I write the schema by hand?
en.x: can i write the schema by hand? yes, in the json tab of “shaped response”. if it keeps failing, simplify it or clarify the fields’ descriptions.

en.ti: The response does not match the JSON Schema
en.x: the response does not match the json schema salida no cumple esquema the response did not have the requested shape. the playground shows which field failed; “correct” asks the agent to fix it. if it keeps failing, simplify the schema.

en.ti: Recipes and fallback
en.x: recipes and fallback a recipe fixes instructions, agent, model, schema and fallback, so your app only sends the message. the recipe instructions, agent and model, effort, schema and fallback. main agent answers if it can. fallback up to 3 agents that take over, in order, if the main one fails before answering. the response history says which agent answered. in the playground write the instructions, for example “always answer in spanish”. pick the main agent and up to 3 fallbacks, each with its own effort if you like. test it with a message and your files; when it works, click “save as api”.

en.ti: How do I make my app answer in a given language?
en.x: how do i make my app answer in a given language? create an api for that app and write in its instructions “always answer in spanish”. they are added to every request without changing the app.

en.ti: What if an agent hits its limit?
en.x: what if an agent hits its limit? if the recipe has a fallback, the next agent takes over. if the agent had already started answering it is not switched, so two answers are never mixed.

en.ti: Does the time limit count per attempt?
en.x: does the time limit count per attempt? yes: each fallback agent gets the full time limit.

en.ti: The provider usage limit was reached
en.x: the provider usage limit was reached limite uso proveedor you hit your plan’s or key’s limit. wait for the provider to reset it or add a fallback to the recipe.

en.ti: Tools
en.x: tools your app offers functions; the agent asks for one with its arguments, and your app runs it and returns the result. your app offers the functions, with a json schema for their arguments. the agent asks a call with arguments already validated. it never runs anything. your app runs it the function, and returns the result in the next message. the response the agent answers using that result. pass your functions in tools (openai and anthropic) or herramientas (native api). if the agent asks for one, run it in your app with the arguments it sends. return the result in the next message (tool or herramienta role) and call again. tool choice (auto, required, none or one function) and parallel calls work as in openai and anthropic. with tools, the response arrives complete at the end, even if you ask for stream.

en.ti: Where is the full example?
en.x: where is the full example? in the developer guide: the whole cycle in python, javascript, go and curl, through all three urls.

en.ti: Can the agent run something on my computer?
en.x: can the agent run something on my computer? no. it only asks for the call; whether to run it is up to your app.

en.ti: Budgets
en.x: budgets set daily or monthly limits for an api or the whole workspace, in requests, tokens or dollars. usage every request adds requests, tokens and, if the agent reports it, dollars. warning at 80% the bar turns yellow. cap at 100% the app gets a 429 error until the next day or month starts. create an api for that app in my apis. in its settings, set a daily or monthly budget in requests, tokens or dollars. if needed, “reset usage” opens it again right away. the dollar limit only adds up the cost the agent reports (claude today). for the whole workspace, add “presupuesto” to the global settings.

en.ti: The budget ran out
en.x: the budget ran out presupuesto agotado that api or the workspace hit its limit (error 429). wait for the day or month to reset, or click “reset usage” in my apis.

en.ti: History
en.x: history every request stays in history with its response, the agent that answered and the log of each step. filter by status, origin or group, or search by text across the whole history. open a request to see the response and its “log”, with every step and its time. if it failed, fix the cause and click “retry”.

en.ti: What do Completed, In progress and With errors mean?
en.x: what do completed, in progress and with errors mean? completed got a response; in progress are waiting or running; with errors failed or were interrupted.

en.ti: Can I follow a request live?
en.x: can i follow a request live? yes: click its tram on the home map and you will see its route (queue, preparation, running, validation and arrival) as it moves.

en.ti: How do I see how long each step took?
en.x: how do i see how long each step took? in “log”, under the response or in the detail: every step with its time and, at the top, how long each stage took.

en.ti: How do I watch what it processes while developing?
en.x: how do i watch what it processes while developing? “tramtai service log -f” shows one live line per request: agent, model, duration, tokens and the api it came from.

en.ti: Can I run the service in the foreground?
en.x: can i run the service in the foreground? yes: stop the service and run “tramtai service start --abrir”: it runs with the log in view, opens the app and ctrl+c stops it.

en.ti: How do I delete test data?
en.x: how do i delete test data? in settings, “delete data” removes the history and the per-app apis. you can also empty history.

en.ti: Workspaces
en.x: workspaces the global one and one per project, each with its own history, apis and settings. global for loose text and files. its settings apply to projects that do not have their own. what is inherited model, history and budget: what a project does not define comes from the global one. a project a folder with .tramtai/: its own history, apis and settings. open a project from the selector at the top or from workspaces. if the folder had no .tramtai/, tramtai prepares it and trusts it. if it already had .tramtai/ (a cloned repository), decide whether you trust it: then its local.yaml can use security settings. in workspaces you see all of them, stopped ones too. stop the ones you do not use and forget the ones you no longer need.

en.ti: What does trusting a folder mean?
en.x: what does trusting a folder mean? that its .tramtai/local.yaml can use security settings, such as each agent’s program. trust is stored in tramtai, never in the repository.

en.ti: Can I move or rename a project?
en.x: can i move or rename a project? yes. its id stays in .tramtai/espacio: at its new path it keeps its history, apis and key. it asks again whether you trust it: trust does not travel with the folder.

en.ti: And if I copy the folder?
en.x: and if i copy the folder? the copy is a new workspace, with its own history and no key until you create one; the original stays as it was.

en.ti: What does “Forget” delete?
en.x: what does “forget” delete? its history, uploaded files, key and api keys in tramtai. the project folder, with its .tramtai/, is not touched.

en.ti: Why does a workspace show “Not found”?
en.x: why does a workspace show “not found”? its folder was moved or deleted. “locate the folder” links it again without losing anything (then “trust” if it uses security settings); “forget” if you no longer need it.

en.ti: How do I know whether a setting is the project’s or the global one?
en.x: how do i know whether a setting is the project’s or the global one? in settings each one says “own” or “from global”. own ones have “back to global”, which removes the value from the project’s local.yaml.

en.ti: And from the terminal?
en.x: and from the terminal? “tramtai workspaces” lists them; “tramtai workspace start”, “stop” and “forget” do the same as the page.

en.ti: You need to decide whether you trust that folder
en.x: you need to decide whether you trust that folder confianza requerida the folder already had a tramtai configuration. decide whether you trust it: if not, it opens without its apis or budget.

en.ti: This project’s workspace is stopped
en.x: this project’s workspace is stopped espacio detenido you are inside a stopped project. start it with tramtai workspace start, or use --global to send to the global one.

en.ti: Keys and APIs
en.x: keys and apis the workspace key and per-app apis: when to use each one and what happens when you regenerate them. how many one per workspace as many as you like what it can use any agent and model what you configure what for your scripts and tests from outside the web ui each real app when regenerated every app that uses it stops connecting only that app stops connecting each per-app api has its own address, budget and history: if one leaks, you revoke only that one.

en.ti: Which key do I give my app?
en.x: which key do i give my app? for your scripts and tests, the workspace one. for a real app, create its own api in my apis: you can limit, measure and revoke it without touching the rest.

en.ti: What if the workspace key leaks?
en.x: what if the workspace key leaks? regenerate it in “workspace key” in my apis, or with “tramtai global token --rotar” (“tramtai project token --rotar” in a project). the old one stops working at once. per-app apis do not change.

en.ti: Where do I see the workspace key?
en.x: where do i see the workspace key? only when you create or regenerate it. a new workspace has no key: create it in “workspace key” in my apis or with “tramtai global token --rotar” (“tramtai project token --rotar” in a project).

en.ti: What if I use the TRAMTAI_TOKEN_GLOBAL variable?
en.x: what if i use the tramtai token global variable? that key cannot be created or regenerated from tramtai, nor from the cli: change it in the variable. “tramtai global token” tells you where it comes from.

en.ti: Why does it suggest creating an API?
en.x: why does it suggest creating an api? because more than 20 app requests used the workspace key in 24 h. it is only a suggestion: everything keeps working the same.

en.ti: Settings and updates
en.x: settings and updates launch at sign-in, default model, files, history and updates. choose how it starts when you sign in: “the app in the tray” or “just the service”, with no window. without signing in, it’s the server (“tramtai-servidor install”), another environment. pick the model and effort used when a request does not say. in history decide how long requests are kept; in files, prepare the converter.

en.ti: What’s the difference between the three ways to start?
en.x: what’s the difference between the three ways to start? the app in the tray and just the service start when you sign in, with your account and your data. the system service starts with the computer and its own account: another environment.

en.ti: What happens when I update?
en.x: what happens when i update? the notice shows what each version brings. with the windows installer it installs itself and the app reopens with your data; otherwise, the notice has the link.

en.ti: How do I update without the Windows installer?
en.x: how do i update without the windows installer? homebrew: “brew upgrade”. the .dmg, .deb, .rpm and portable: the new package on top. in the terminal, “tramtai update” (“--comprobar” only checks).

en.ti: Can I check for a version now?
en.x: can i check for a version now? yes: “check for updates now” in settings. tramtai checks every hour (only github’s public page); turn it off in settings → check for updates.

en.ti: Which version do I have?
en.x: which version do i have? open “about tramtai” in the side menu or the tray; “copy support details” copies what is needed, without keys.

en.ti: Where is my data kept?
en.x: where is my data kept? only on this computer: %appdata%\tramtai (windows), ~/library/application support/tramtai (macos) or ~/.config/tramtai (linux); the portable, in “datos-tramtai”.

en.ti: Can I go back to an earlier version?
en.x: can i go back to an earlier version? once you’ve run v0.56, v0.55 or earlier won’t open your workspaces: it says the database isn’t supported. nothing is deleted; with v0.56 or later everything is still there.

en.ti: How long is it kept?
en.x: how long is it kept? responses, 24 hours; the rest of the history, 7 days, up to 10,000 requests. change it in settings → history, where you can also delete it.

en.ti: What are “This workspace” and “All of Tramtai”?
en.x: what are “this workspace” and “all of tramtai”? “this workspace” keeps the model, history and data of the open workspace; “all of tramtai”, the port, converter, updates and startup.

en.ti: How do I sign in to the server from another computer?
en.x: how do i sign in to the server from another computer? with the administrator password and, if you turn it on, two-step verification, over https only. they change in settings → security; on linux, totp only with “tramtai-servidor admin”.

en.ti: Server mode
en.x: server mode a system-wide tramtai that starts with the computer, with nobody signed in, and opens from other computers over https. install it as administrator: “sudo ./tramtai server install” from the linux .tar.gz, “sudo tramtai-servidor install” after the .deb or .rpm, or in an administrator console on windows. set the administrator password with “tramtai-servidor admin password”: without it, nobody signs in from other computers. totp, with “… admin totp enable”. open it to the network over https only: behind a proxy (recommended), with your own certificate or with let’s encrypt. the server guide has an example per proxy. store the agents’ keys on the server with “tramtai-servidor keys set <name>”: never from the web ui. you manage it on the server itself with “tramtai-servidor <command>” (with sudo on linux). it doesn’t hide your user’s tramtai, which is another environment. notice your account with a provider may be limited, suspended or closed if you use your subscription with tramtai, and the provider may change its rules without notice. the author cannot recover it. tramtai’s conditions (totp, one request at a time) lower the risk but do not remove it, and they are not a legal opinion on the provider’s terms. what you open to the network is your responsibility: https, firewall, passwords, backups and updates. if other people use your server, you answer for their data under the law that applies to you. tramtai is free and provided as is, without warranties. the full terms: “tramtai-servidor terms”, or the link in about tramtai.

en.ti: What is server mode?
en.x: what is server mode? a system-wide tramtai, separate from yours: it starts with the computer, without a session, with its own account, data and port. on linux with systemd and on windows server; not on macos.

en.ti: Why won’t it start with permitir_remoto over HTTP?
en.x: why won’t it start with permitir remoto over http? because the keys and the password would travel unencrypted. outside this computer, https only: a proxy, your certificate (servicio.tls.modo: archivos) or let’s encrypt.

en.ti: Which proxy do I use?
en.x: which proxy do i use? the one you already have: the guide covers caddy, nginx, apache, traefik, haproxy and iis. put its address in servicio.proxy.confiables and your domain in servicio.dominios.

en.ti: And on my local network, without HTTPS?
en.x: and on my local network, without https? no plain http there either: the password and keys would travel unencrypted. use tailscale serve, caddy with its internal ca, your own ca’s certificate (mkcert) or an ssh tunnel; see the guide.

en.ti: And from the server itself?
en.x: and from the server itself? “tramtai-servidor open”, the w key and the app come in through the local entrance. with trusted proxies, opening the public port by hand on the server counts as coming from outside.

en.ti: Where do the agents’ keys go?
en.x: where do the agents’ keys go? encrypted: on windows, in the service account’s store; on linux, with systemd-creds. the service key, with the server open to the network, only works from the server itself.

en.ti: Who runs the agents?
en.x: who runs the agents? the service, with its account. plain “sudo tramtai-servidor agents” (the diagnosis), “ejecutar” without the service and “servicio iniciar” in the foreground are refused; “agents login” works.

en.ti: How do I install the agents on the server?
en.x: how do i install the agents on the server? from agents in the remote web ui, the terminal or “tramtai-servidor agents install”: tramtai installs, updates and uninstalls their clis with the service account. administrator only.

en.ti: What if sign-in can’t be done from Tramtai?
en.x: what if sign-in can’t be done from tramtai? on linux, the notice gives the command to do it as the service account. on windows server that account has no console: it can’t be done by hand, so use the agent’s api key.

en.ti: Can I connect my tools?
en.x: can i connect my tools? not here: server mode doesn’t offer claude code, codex, continue, opencode or kilo code. connect them from tramtai with your normal user, outside server mode.

en.ti: Can I use my subscription on the server?
en.x: can i use my subscription on the server? by default, an api key. open to the network, only the personal subscription: with totp, for you and one request at a time by default (up to 3 with suscripcion simultaneas).

en.ti: How do I turn on my subscription on the server?
en.x: how do i turn on my subscription on the server? sign in with “tramtai-servidor agents login <id>” and, when it’s done, turn it on with “tramtai-servidor agents subscription <id>” (open to the network, with --personal). one, then the other.

en.ti: What’s the risk with Codex on the server?
en.x: what’s the risk with codex on the server? it reads what the service account reads, keys included. give the workspace key only to people you trust and, in other people’s apis, set allowed models and fallback without codex (empty allows any).

en.ti: How do I update it?
en.x: how do i update it? “tramtai-servidor update” checks the signature, lets requests finish and swaps the program. if you installed it with the .deb or .rpm, update with apt or dnf.

en.ti: How do I remove it?
en.x: how do i remove it? “tramtai-servidor uninstall” removes the service and the program and keeps the data; with “--delete-data” it also deletes the data, the keys and the account.

en.ti: Two environments
en.x: two environments your tramtai and the server’s share nothing: each has its own apis, keys, cli sessions, history and settings. starts when you sign in (the app in the tray or just the service) or when you open it with the computer, with nobody signed in account yours tramtai on linux; nt service\tramtai on windows data your tramtai folder (in the portable copy, “datos-tramtai”) /var/lib/tramtai on linux; %programdata%\tramtai on windows agents’ keys your session’s encrypted store the service account’s (windows) or systemd-creds (linux), set with the cli managed with “tramtai …”, the app, the terminal and the web ui “tramtai-servidor …” as administrator, and the web ui web ui from another computer no, by default: it listens on 127.0.0.1 yes, over https and with the administrator password nothing moves from one to the other: a workspace, api or key of yours doesn’t exist on the server, or the other way around. each environment accepts the terms on its own.

en.ti: How do I know which one I’m in?
en.x: how do i know which one i’m in? the web ui header and the terminal’s status line say “server” or “this device”. about shows the environment, the account and the folder.

en.ti: Can I move my APIs to the server?
en.x: can i move my apis to the server? they aren’t copied: create them again on the server, with their keys. that way a key from your computer never opens the server, or the other way around.

en.ti: Why does it warn me about another Tramtai, a system one?
en.x: why does it warn me about another tramtai, a system one? because the system service also runs on this computer, on another port. it’s another environment, with its own apis and keys: there’s nothing to do.

en.ti: Which one does the CLI talk to?
en.x: which one does the cli talk to? “tramtai …” talks to yours; “tramtai-servidor …” (or “tramtai --server …”) to the system one, and every output that changes something starts with “server:”.

en.ti: Why does it ask me to accept the terms again?
en.x: why does it ask me to accept the terms again? each environment keeps its own acceptance: your computer’s doesn’t count for the server, which asks for it when you install it.

en.ti: Something failed
en.x: something failed the most common errors, with the same title you see in the app, and what to do about each. open history and click the request with the error. find its error below: each one says what it means and what to do. open “log” to see which agent was tried, the warnings and how long it took. fix the cause and click “retry”.

en.ti: Offline
en.x: offline sin conexion the service is not running. open the app or run “tramtai service start”. with start-up in settings it starts on its own when you sign in.

en.ti: The key is missing or not valid
en.x: the key is missing or not valid no autorizado check the key in your app: the workspace one or that api’s. if you regenerated it, the old one no longer works.

en.ti: The agent has no valid session or key
en.x: the agent has no valid session or key autenticacion agente the agent has no session or key. in agents, sign in to its cli or save an api key.

en.ti: The agent is not available
en.x: the agent is not available agente no disponible the cli is not installed or cannot be found; agents says how to install it. antigravity also cannot be used from apis.

en.ti: The provider usage limit was reached
en.x: the provider usage limit was reached limite uso proveedor you hit your plan’s or key’s limit. wait for the provider to reset it or add a fallback to the recipe.

en.ti: That model is not available
en.x: that model is not available modelo no disponible use a model from the list with the agent in front, for example claude/sonnet, or a profile like perfil/rapido.

en.ti: A parameter is not supported
en.x: a parameter is not supported parametro no soportado you asked for something terminal agents cannot honor (images, n above 1, stop…): remove it. unknown ones are accepted with compatibilidad.modo tolerante.

en.ti: The input does not fit in the model
en.x: the input does not fit in the model entrada demasiado grande the documents do not fit the model. send fewer pages, split the file or put a model with more context in the fallback.

en.ti: The budget ran out
en.x: the budget ran out presupuesto agotado that api or the workspace hit its limit (error 429). wait for the day or month to reset, or click “reset usage” in my apis.

en.ti: The response does not match the JSON Schema
en.x: the response does not match the json schema salida no cumple esquema the response did not have the requested shape. the playground shows which field failed; “correct” asks the agent to fix it. if it keeps failing, simplify the schema.

en.ti: The time limit ran out
en.x: the time limit ran out tiempo ejecucion agotado it took longer than the time limit. raise it in the playground’s advanced options or in the request, or lower the effort.

en.ti: The queue is full; try again shortly
en.x: the queue is full; try again shortly cola llena too many requests at once. retry in a few seconds: the response carries retry-after with the wait.

en.ti: The file could not be converted
en.x: the file could not be converted conversion fallida a file could not be converted. check that it is not damaged or password-protected and that its format is accepted.

en.ti: The file converter is missing
en.x: the file converter is missing conversor no disponible the file converter is missing: settings → files → “prepare files”. if your network blocks the download, use the converter package for windows.

en.ti: The agent returned an error
en.x: the agent returned an error error agente the agent failed while answering. open “log” to see its message; retry, or add a fallback to the recipe so another agent takes over.

en.ti: The agent response could not be understood
en.x: the agent response could not be understood error protocolo agente the cli answered something tramtai does not understand; it usually happens after updating the cli. update tramtai or try another agent.

en.ti: It waited too long in the queue
en.x: it waited too long in the queue tiempo cola agotado the request waited too long for its turn because there were many at once. retry in a moment or send fewer requests together.

en.ti: That API does not allow that model
en.x: that api does not allow that model modelo no permitido that api only accepts certain models. use one of its own or add that model to its allowed list in my apis.

en.ti: No model is configured for that profile
en.x: no model is configured for that profile modelo no configurado the requested profile (for example perfil/rapido) has no model for that agent. pick a specific model, like claude/sonnet.

en.ti: The space for files is full
en.x: the space for files is full cuota cargas agotada the space for uploaded files is full. wait for older ones to expire or delete data in settings.

en.ti: That agent is disconnected
en.x: that agent is disconnected agente desconectado that agent is disconnected. connect it in agents or choose another model; the fallback skips it.

en.ti: You need to decide whether you trust that folder
en.x: you need to decide whether you trust that folder confianza requerida the folder already had a tramtai configuration. decide whether you trust it: if not, it opens without its apis or budget.

en.ti: This project’s workspace is stopped
en.x: this project’s workspace is stopped espacio detenido you are inside a stopped project. start it with tramtai workspace start, or use --global to send to the global one.

en.ti: Concepts
en.x: concepts the words tramtai uses, one line each.

en.ti: Agent
en.x: agent the ai that answers: claude code, codex, github copilot, the gemini api or antigravity. connect it in agents, with your subscription or an api key.

en.ti: Model
en.x: model the model the agent uses (sonnet, opus, gpt-5.5…). it is written agent/model; the list shows the exact version behind it.

en.ti: Profile
en.x: profile a shortcut like perfil/rapido or perfil/profundo that picks the right model of the default agent, without typing its name.

en.ti: Effort
en.x: effort how hard the model reasons before answering, from low to maximum. more effort gives better responses to hard questions but takes longer and uses more tokens.

en.ti: Recipe
en.x: recipe what defines how an api answers: instructions, agent and model, effort, fallback and json schema. you test it in the playground.

en.ti: Fallback
en.x: fallback up to 3 backup agents that take over the request if the main one fails before it starts answering.

en.ti: Workspace key and per-app APIs
en.x: workspace key and per-app apis the main one serves everything with a single key. a per-app api has its own url, key, recipe and budget.

en.ti: Request
en.x: request each message sent to an agent, from the playground, the terminal or an app. it stays in the history with its response and its log.

en.ti: Shaped response (JSON schema)
en.x: shaped response (json schema) the shape the response must have: its fields and their type. if the response does not match, the request fails or a correction is asked for, instead of delivering something unexpected.

en.ti: Context
en.x: context how much text a model accepts at once. converted documents count: if they do not fit, tramtai says so before spending tokens.

en.ti: Workspace
en.x: workspace where requests and apis are kept: the global one, or one per project with its own history.

en.ti: Budget
en.x: budget daily and monthly limits in requests, tokens or dollars, for one api or for the whole workspace.

en.ti: Do requests end up as chats in Claude Code, Codex or GitHub Copilot?
en.x: do requests end up as chats in claude code, codex or github copilot? no. tramtai runs each cli without saving the session, so your chats don’t fill up; the log stays only in tramtai’s history.

en.ti: Does Tramtai send my data to a server?
en.x: does tramtai send my data to a server? it has no server of its own. your messages only go to the provider of the agent you pick, as if you used its cli.

en.ti: Can I use it at my company?
en.x: can i use it at my company? it is free for personal, non-commercial use (polyform noncommercial 1.0.0). a company or commercial product needs a separate license: write to me.

en.ti: What if the port is busy?
en.x: what if the port is busy? tramtai uses the next free one and says so; the app and cli find it on their own, but your apps must use the new address. set it in settings.

en.ti: How do I uninstall it?
en.x: how do i uninstall it? windows: settings → apps → tramtai (it asks whether to delete your data). macos: to the trash or “brew uninstall --cask --zap tramtai”. linux: apt or dnf remove tramtai.

en.ti: What it is
en.x: what it is the same tramtai, installed as a system service on linux with systemd or windows server (server core too). it has its own unprivileged account, its data in a system folder and its own port. macos has no system service: there you have “just the service”, which starts when you sign in.

en.ti: Two environments
en.x: two environments your tramtai and the server’s share nothing: each has its own workspaces, apis, keys, cli sessions, history and settings. an api on your computer doesn’t exist on the server, or the other way around. the web ui header and the terminal always say which one you’re in: “server” or “this device”.

en.ti: Notice
en.x: notice before installing, the server asks you to accept the terms by typing “acepto” (spanish for “i accept”). these are the five risks you take on:

en.ti: Install
en.x: install linux. download your architecture’s .tar.gz (amd64 or arm64) and sha256sums.txt from releases, check the sum and install as root. or install the server package (tramtai-…-servidor-linux-….deb or .rpm), which lives next to the desktop one, and then sudo tramtai-servidor install: the package alone starts nothing, because you have to accept the terms first.

en.ti: Open to the network
en.x: open to the network after installing, the server only serves this same computer. to use it from others, always with https: if you open it to the network without it, it won’t start, because your keys would travel unencrypted. there are three ways:

en.ti: Administrator
en.x: administrator set the administrator password (12 characters or more) on the server with tramtai-servidor admin password; only a hash of it is stored. the second factor (totp), with your authenticator app and 10 recovery codes, is turned on with … admin totp enable or, on windows, also in settings → security. after 5 failed attempts, that address waits 15 minutes, and sessions expire after 12 hours idle.

en.ti: Keys and subscription
en.x: keys and subscription agents’ keys are stored encrypted, on the server and with the cli (tramtai-servidor keys set anthropic api key), never from the web ui. tramtai installs the agents’ clis for the service account (tramtai-servidor agents install claude), or the ones you already installed for the whole computer will do; the service runs them with its own account.

en.ti: Update and remove
en.x: update and remove the server tells you when there’s a new version. tramtai-servidor update checks tramtai’s signature, lets running requests finish and swaps the program; if you installed the package, update with apt or dnf. tramtai-servidor uninstall removes it and keeps your data; --delete-data also deletes the data, the keys and the account.

en.ti: If something fails
en.x: if something fails the full server guide, with the settings for each case, and the help: server mode and two environments.

en.ti: Get started
en.x: get started you need tramtai running with at least one agent connected, plus your api’s url and key (in the app, my apis). the examples read them from three variables: tramtai url (default http://127.0.0.1:17373), tramtai key and tramtai model (agent and model, default claude/haiku).

en.ti: Your first message
en.x: your first message through the openai-compatible url, with the response streamed live. the model field picks agent and model.

en.ti: Files
en.x: files accepted: pdf, word (.docx), powerpoint (.pptx), excel (.xlsx) and html, which tramtai turns into text, and plain text as is (.txt, .md, .json, .csv, .xml, .yaml…). through openai and anthropic the file goes in base64 inside the message (about 12 mb in total); through the native api you upload it to /cargas (up to 50 mb each) and the request cites it. the exact list is at get /api/v1/limites.

en.ti: JSON responses
en.x: json responses ask for the response with a json schema: tramtai validates it before returning it and, if it does not match, can ask the agent to fix it.

en.ti: Tool calling
en.x: tool calling tools are functions of your app: look up an order, search your database, check the weather. you describe them to the agent; if it needs one, it asks for the call with its arguments, your app runs it and sends back the result in the next turn. the agent never runs anything: it only asks.

en.ti: Long requests
en.x: long requests native api only (the trabajos resource): you create the request, follow it live through events (if the connection drops, resume with last-event-id) and read the response. post /trabajos/{id}/cancelar cancels it and post /trabajos/{id}/reintentar sends it again.

en.ti: Follow what happens
en.x: follow what happens get /api/v1/eventos is an sse stream for the whole workspace: it starts with the requests in progress (and those finished less than 10 s ago) and then reports every stage change (cola, preparacion, ejecucion, validacion, llegada) with the agent, model and source api; intento is the request’s own: 1 with the main agent and 1 more each time the fallback switches agent. the service stores it, so it is right even if you connect after the switch. a foto event marks the end of that first snapshot: anything you had that did not come has finished. it never carries the message, the response or the files. with a per-app api key, only that api’s requests arrive. handy for your own dashboard; it is what the home map uses.

en.ti: Errors and retries
en.x: errors and retries errors arrive in the format of the api you use, with a stable code. to retry without duplicating a request, send the idempotency-key header: the same key with the same request returns that same request instead of a new one (on all three apis).

en.ti: Import into Postman or generate a client
en.x: import into postman or generate a client get /api/v1/openapi.json describes the native api in openapi 3.1, with your workspace’s or your api’s url. postman, insomnia or bruno import it as is (“import” → url or file), and openapi-generator or openapi-typescript generate a client. in the app, the “which url do i use?” guide in my apis (and each api’s detail) downloads it as a file.

en.ti: Limits
en.x: limits get /api/v1/limites gives a request’s caps (files, sizes, messages) and the accepted formats, so your app knows them before sending.

en.ti: Manage from the terminal
en.x: manage from the terminal tramtai terminal (or just tramtai) has the same pages as the app: home, agents, playground, my apis, history, workspaces, settings (with what’s new and about) and help. it talks to the service through its admin api, so it doesn’t need the app open. on another computer, ssh into the computer where tramtai runs and open it there: by default, the service only serves 127.0.0.1. in server mode, sudo tramtai-servidor opens the server’s terminal.
